items.root_cause: test-guards Check/CheckScript/CheckWarn (test-guards.ps1:190-218) DISCARD the captured child output on FAIL, so a failing case cannot name the guard that actually fired, and a leaked mutation (a restore that did not take effect) is invisible - the suite reports exit-code mismatches instead of evidence. The instrument is blind to its own failure cause; that is why the same 5 failures have sat undiagnosed since 08-29.

surface_fix.what: make failures carry their evidence, then fix the leaking restore it exposes
surface_fix.exact_change: On FAIL, Check/CheckScript/CheckWarn print the captured output ($o) - at least every line matching HARD FAIL|WARN|FAIL. Add a residue tripwire: each case records Get-FileHash of every file it mutated, and after its inline restore asserts the hash equals the backup hash, naming the first mismatch. Then re-run hermetically; the case-16 output will name the guard that is red, which identifies the leaking case (window: after case 15 multibuy, at or before case 16 tile-integrity). Fix that restore. Expect 30/30.

items.root_fix_note: surface_fix IS the root fix: the evidence capture is the structural change, the leaking restore is the instance it will expose.

items.subject: Recipe price inversion: 2 clamped
evidence: Current manifest (v2-perserving.json, 08-29 16:44): exactly 3 clamped rows, each with cheapest_ps==everyday_ps (the clamp signature): cochinita-pibil-pork-rice-bowls ev 2.00, harissa-chicken-rice-bowls ev 3.15, tunisian-harissa-coconut-beef-meatballs ev 4.16. philly-cheesesteak-stuffed-peppers NO LONGER inverts - its driver was the shaved-beef basis bug, fixed (see 8360b4).

The underlying cells, quoted from comparison-2026-08-26: harissa-paste | Walmart | "(12 pack) Mina, Harissa Spicy Moroccan Red Pepper Sauce , 10 Fl oz" | 120 oz | $59.76 | $0.498/oz vs Hy-Vee runner-up $6.3105/oz (12.7x). achiote-paste | Walmart | "Chef Merito Achiote Condimentado Spiced Annatto Seed Paste, 3.5 oz, (Pack of 12)" | 42 oz | $16.24 | $0.3867/oz - the commodity's ONLY cell, and cochinita pibil is the achiote recipe. All three inversions are ONE mechanism: Walmart marketplace CASE listings win the per-oz crown, and cheapest_ps bills the recipe the whole case package.

Why NO rule ships today, measured not guessed: 30 board cells declare 6+ packs and the class is not uniformly wrong (batteries 66-pack, bottled water 24-pack, Kleenex 16-pack are legitimately case-sold), so a size-shape heuristic misfires; and a known-wrong ruling on the Chef Merito case would orphan achiote-paste (only cell) and silently DROP cochinita's cost line in cost-recipes - a wrong-lower published number, worse than the clamp. Two more marketplace cases sit one price move from a crown: cajun-seasoning@Walmart "(6 pack) Tony Chachere's, 192 oz" $33.28 at 0.1733 vs Sam's 0.1666 crown, and canned-mixed-vegetables@Walmart "(6 pack) Great Value, 15 oz" IS the crown at 0.064/oz.

items.root_cause: First-match-wins plus one-word produce includes (\bapple(s)?\b, \bonion, \bcelery\b) let prepared/deli products whose names carry a produce word steal candidates from later commodities, invisibly - the stolen name usually cannot win the thief's cell either. Fixes belong on the THIEF; where the product belongs to NEITHER commodity, on both, plus a reviewed allowlist entry so the audit stops re-paging the store.

items.resolution_note: All 57 semantic findings dispositioned: 13 admits measured over 29,155 names (39 routing changes total with item 14416d, zero unintended, positive control reproduced); two DEAD commodities (chili-garlic-sauce, frozen-cauliflower-florets - includes require a globally-excluded word with no relax) revived and now carry 3-store rows; ~28 known-wrong rulings recorded so the sweep stops re-paging; 4 identity calls to Brad. firm-tofu crown moves to Aldi; frozen-fruit moves down at three stores on real prices; a popsicle hijack and a sugared-fruit admit were caught by the measurement and fenced before shipping.
items.premise_verified: TRUE on both structural finds, verified 2026-08-30 07:35-07:53 by reading the rules rather than trusting the summary. STRUCTURAL FIND 1 CONFIRMED: chili-garlic-sauce (index 585) has NO relax_global key at all and both its includes require the literal word sauce; frozen-cauliflower-florets (index 565) has NO relax_global and its single include is ^(?=.*\bfrozen\b)(?=.*\bcauliflower\s+florets?\b).*$. GLOBAL_EXCLUDE at compare-deals.ps1:1755 carries both '\bsauce\b' and '\bfrozen\b', and match-lib.ps1:23 states relax_global waives a global token by EXACT pattern-string equality, so both commodities were structurally unmatchable and both carry zero board cells today. The clean twin holds: teriyaki-sauce (index 381) already carries relax_global ['\bsauce\b'] and has a 6-store row. STRUCTURAL FIND 2 CONFIRMED AND EXTENDED: the sweep re-pages deliberate excludes, and it also re-pages products that are ALREADY RULED - two of the 42 rulings in this batch (Smithfield Steakhouse seasoned tenderloin, Jimmy Dean roll-ups) came back "an entry with that key already exists", so the sweep reads neither the excludes nor known-wrong.json. Same no-memory mechanism the plan names, one layer wider; recorded, not treated as new. POPSICLE GUARD PREMISE CONFIRMED BY INDEX: frozen-fruit is index 273 and popsicles is index 274, so first-match-wins genuinely reaches frozen-fruit FIRST and the (?!\s*pop) guard is load-bearing exactly as the plan says. ONE FINDING THE PLAN DOES NOT DISPOSITION: semantic finding 16, "Friendly Farms Almond Original Milk" at Aldi under almond-milk. Not acted on, and no rule invented for it: Aldi ALREADY holds the almond-milk cell and the crown at $0.0358/floz with "Friendly Farms Original Almond Milk", so this is a second spelling of a covered commodity, not a gap. Left for the next sweep rather than shipping a rule the artifact never measured.
items.deviation:
ALL THE PLANNED WORK SHIPPED, with two measured deviations and one BOUNCE.

SHIPPED: 23 of the 24 rule_edits (see the revert below), verified byte-level as 20 commodities changed, 24 patterns added, ZERO removed, zero commodities added or lost. Both DEAD commodities are alive and carry 3-store rows exactly as predicted: chili-garlic-sauce Bakers 0.3113 / Walmart 0.48 / Family Fare 0.7488, frozen-cauliflower-florets Walmart 0.0967 / Bakers 0.1852 / Family Fare 0.2492. 42 known-wrong rulings recorded (39 new, 3 already present under keys that cover them). The root_fix shipped as grocery/dead-commodity-lib.ps1 plus 9 cases in test-auditors.ps1 (run daily in production by check-ad-cycles), with the frozen PRE-FIX rulesets as must-fire fixtures and five clean twins.

DEVIATION 1 - ONE RULE EDIT REVERTED, on a hard guard's evidence. coconut-oil.include += '\bcoconut\s+cooking\s+oil\b' was applied, then removed. Measured upside on the board: ZERO - the artifact itself records coconut-oil Walmart 0.2434 -> 0.2434 NO MOVE. Measured downside: it changed which Sams capture COVERS coconut-oil, flipping the Sams cell from Carrington Refined 128 fl oz at 0.1952 (explicitly VOLUME-sized) onto Members Mark Organic Virgin 56oz at 0.1961 (WEIGHT-sized), and guards.ps1 hard-failed it via audit-unit-basis-outlier: "[CROWN ON A WEIGHT ROW] Coconut Oil Sams Club 0.1961 /oz size='56 oz' (row is priced by volume)". The guard was right. No threshold was touched and nothing was allowlisted; the rule came out. After the revert guards read hard=0 warn=24 and the Sams cell is back at 0.1952 on the correctly-sized row.

DEVIATION 2 - TWO frozen-fruit cells landed CHEAPER than predicted, both on real rows, both verified by arithmetic. Sams predicted 0.1433 (MM Blueberries 4 lb, $9.17) but landed 0.1247 on "Members Mark Natural Sliced Strawberries, Frozen, 4 lbs." $7.98/64 oz, from sams-deals-2026-08-15 which is inside the 90-day union but was NOT in the artifact's corpus (the artifact routed only sams-deals-2026-08-29). Family Fare predicted 0.2806 (Mango Chunks) but landed 0.2748 on "Our Family Blueberries, Fresh Frozen 40 Oz" $10.99/40 oz, as_of 2026-08-30 - a row that did not exist when the artifact was frozen at 06:45, and the ONE name my pre-flight re-diff flagged as outside the contract before I touched anything. Both moves are DOWN, both are the intended token doing its job, and audit-capture-eviction returns 0 findings on the rebuilt board.

NET: 13 board cells moved, 11 exactly as the plan predicted, 2 cheaper than predicted on named real rows, 0 unintended. Three commodities gained their first row ever.

BOUNCE (new failure class):
NEW FAILURE CLASS FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING, WITH THE MEASUREMENT (not an observation). A commodity whose declared UNIT is not in the engine's unit vocabulary can never hold a board cell, however well its rules match. This is NOT the dead-commodity class this item fixed: there the MATCHER can never keep a row; here the matcher keeps the row and the PRICER can never turn it into a cell. From outside they are identical - zero cells, which reads as a commodity Omaha does not carry - and the new dead-commodity check does not catch it (it reports 0 dead after the fix while these 7 stay unpriceable).

PROVEN FROM THE SOURCE: compare-deals.ps1 Convert-ToUnit (line 142) is a switch over exactly six unit values - lb, oz, floz, gallon, each, dozen - with NO default arm, so any other value falls through to `return $null`. No canonical amount means no per-unit price means no cell, on every row, forever.

PROVEN FROM THE DATA, over all 592 commodities against comparison-2026-08-30: unit 'floz' 74 commodities, 74 with board cells. Unit 'fl_oz' 5 commodities, ZERO with board cells: garlic-infused-olive-oil, coconut-aminos, avocado-oil, peanut-oil, creamy-cilantro-lime-dressing. Unit 'sq_ft' 1 (aluminum-foil), zero cells. Unit 'gram' 1 (saffron), zero cells. A perfect separation on a one-character difference in a data field.

HOW IT SURFACED: this plan predicted coconut-aminos would gain its FIRST cell at Baker's, 0.799 (Bragg $7.99/10 fl oz). The rule change worked exactly as measured - compare-deals -Explain reports the Bragg row as OURS, kept - and the commodity still has no row on the rebuilt board, because its unit is 'fl_oz'.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE, and this is the whole reason it is a bounce rather than a same-day fix. Correcting seven unit fields would create cells at up to seven stores each, and not one of those cells is in the frozen routing artifact, so their blast radius is unmeasured. Five of the seven are OILS, where weight-vs-volume is exactly the basis class this estate keeps getting burned by (see the teriyaki-sauce Aldi ruling on this same board). Shipping a guard for it today was also refused: with the seven still broken the guard would be red on day one, and a guard that is red on day one is one people learn to ignore. The fix and its guard belong together, in a round that measures the cells.

items.subject: store-registry drift - 19 issue(s)
evidence: Re-ran audit-store-registry.ps1 2026-08-30 ~07:40: rc=2, now 21 issues; the 08-22 body's line numbers are stale (the capture-watchdog finding moved from :263 to :432 after the 08-25 rewrite - :263 is now a comment).

They are CONSUMED by live builds: input-usage.json shows hunter-walmart-regular-2026-08-16.json first_used 08-21, last_used the 08-26 build, uses=5. Deleting them would silently drop adjudicated cells.

THREE of the 14 code findings are PHANTOM PAIRS: derive-not-carried.ps1:46+47, price-table-lib.ps1:47+48, test-rollback-ttl.ps1:49+50 are each ONE complete 7-store map split across two source lines (verified derive-not-carried:45-48 by eye - the ordered hashtable names all seven stores); the auditor parses per LINE, so each half reports the other half's stores missing.

Spot-checked the highest-stakes remaining finding: audit-ad-status.ps1:87's three-store list is a FORMAT branch (Hy-Vee/Aldi/Family Fare rows live inside the combined ads file and need per-store filtering; the other stores have per-store files) - a legitimate subset needing documentation, not watchdog blindness.
items.root_cause: Two causes: (1) a real producer (Recipe Hunter promotions) was never registered in stores.json, so its seven files page daily and guard 6 cannot classify them; (2) audit-store-registry's code scan is LINE-scoped, so any store map wrapped across lines produces phantom missing-store findings - 6 of the current 14 code findings are this shape and the count grows every time a line wraps.

surface_fix.what: register the hunter prefix; document genuine subsets
surface_fix.exact_change: stores.json: register hunter-<store> as a regular_prefix class (one-shot promoted captures; no collapse history expected - also settles guard 6's cannot-evaluate warns). allowed_subset entries with reasons for the confirmed-deliberate subsets: audit-ad-status.ps1 combined-ads branch, capture-policy-lib.ps1:659, capture-run.ps1:269 (browser lane), capture-watchdog.ps1:432, rollback-ttl-lib.ps1:60 (dated-capture stores), probe-price-fields.ps1:218, test-capture-builders.ps1:82/89 and test-rollback-ttl fixtures. The developer confirms each line IS deliberate before documenting; any that is not gets rewritten to iterate stores.json.

root_fix.what: statement-scoped store-list parsing in the registry audit
root_fix.exact_change: join continuation lines (or scan the enclosing statement/hashtable) before extracting store names, so a complete map split across lines yields zero findings.

items.premise_verified: PARTLY FALSE, measured 2026-08-30 07:37-07:42. Confirmed: 21 findings; hunter-* files are a legitimate producer (input-usage hunter-walmart uses=5, last_used the 2026-08-26 build). FALSIFIED, sub-premise 1: the plan says THREE phantom pairs; there are TWO. derive-not-carried.ps1:46+47 and price-table-lib.ps1:47+48 are each one hashtable wrapped across two lines (read 45-48 and 46-49 by eye) and the statement-scoped parser silences them: 21 -> 17, exactly 4 findings removed. test-rollback-ttl.ps1:49+50 are NOT one map - they are two separate one-line statements ($allowed = 3 stores that may be given a TTL, $refused = the 4 that must not), which together happen to partition the seven. They correctly still fire and are documented as allowed_subsets instead, which is what the plan's own allowed_subset list already prescribed. FALSIFIED, sub-premise 2: registering the hunter prefix does NOT settle guard 6's cannot-evaluate warns. Guard 6 (guards.ps1:897-900) enumerates prefixes from the FILES it finds under out\regular, not from stores.json, so the registry cannot reach it. That warn is also correct on its merits - each hunter prefix holds exactly one capture, so there genuinely is no history to compare a thin file against - and silencing it would have been weakening a guard to make a run look clean. Left standing and documented in stores.json. All ten remaining code findings read line by line and confirmed deliberate before documenting. Final: audit-store-registry rc=0, 21 -> 0.
